outcome: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN) severity index (Minimal, Mild, Moderate, Severe)
Length of hospital stay at birth
cohort: The study included neonates diagnosed with Rhesus antigen hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn within the first 30 days of life, identified from two commercial insurance claims databases in the United States between 2000 and 2022.
finding: Although most neonates affected by Rhesus antigen alloantibody-induced hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn required only phototherapy, nearly 7% experienced severe disease necessitating invasive intervention or resulting in neonatal mortality.
mod_finding: Severely affected neonates were more frequently delivered by cesarean section.
gest_age: Severely affected neonates had a lower average gestational age (34.1-35.4 weeks) compared to minimally affected neonates (38.4-38.5 weeks).
